source.title: Deep neural networks have an inbuilt Occam’s razor
source.authors: Chris Mingard; H. Rees; Guillermo Valle-Pérez; A. Louis

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on datasets with randomly corrupted labels and measures test generalization, using the label-noise intervention in a new dataset and model setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports MNIST label-corruption results in Figures 3(d–f) and S19. Its discussion of random-label fitting by Zhang et al. is cited prior work, not a result from this study. Generalization-error values for the MNIST corruption experiments are shown only in figures.
record.test_reason: The study reports perfect training accuracy under several MNIST label-corruption levels, directly testing the fitting component of V4 in fully connected tanh networks. Figure S16 also includes randomly generated Boolean targets relevant to V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors argue that structured data and an architectural bias toward simple functions, strong enough to counteract the exponential growth in their number, explain first-order generalization. They present MNIST and CIFAR-10 results as consistent with the Boolean-model account.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains fully connected tanh networks with SGD on MNIST label-corruption conditions and evaluates test generalization; it does not reproduce the original random-label image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight initialization standard deviation and label-corruption level are varied; the figures also distinguish network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Stronger simplicity bias improves generalization on simpler targets; its advantage decreases as target complexity increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization depends on alignment between the network's inductive bias and target structure.

record.problems: The MNIST test-error results relevant to label corruption are presented in scatterplots without textual numeric values. The reported corruption levels do not include 100%.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the only relevant test-error outcomes are figure-only, and the text does not state numerical values or explicitly describe their trend across corruption levels.

untested.parts: The supplied text does not establish zero training error and chance test error together for the completely random Boolean targets in Figure S16, or verify unchanged training hyperparameters relative to true labels.
No training-time comparison between true and random labels or convergence-time measurements across corruption fractions.
No fitting experiments on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Complete label corruption is not tested in the MNIST corruption series. The supplied figure text cannot establish a steady test-error rise toward chance or quantify preservation of the remaining signal.
No controlled tests of weight decay, dropout or data augmentation establishing either necessity or sufficiency.
No measurements separating the learning trajectories of real patterns and noisy labels; the discussion of simpler patterns being learned first cites other studies.

missing.what: Extract the explicitly stated 100% training accuracy for each MNIST corruption condition. These numerical training outcomes are missing despite rows_left_out describing the relevant outcomes as figure-only.

The record overlooks experiments with completely random Boolean targets. Capture their training and test outcomes if recoverable; the supplied text does not provide readable values sufficient for a V1 verdict.
missing.locator: Figure S16(d), (h), (l): random targets, training sizes 1024, 4096 and 16384; 10-layer tanh FCNs with width 256

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to repair. Perfect training accuracy is an extractable result even though training stops when it is first achieved; it does not establish convergence speed. No verdict about a monotonic test-error trend can be justified from scatterplot axes and captions alone.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report fitting a completely random labeling with test error at chance.
The study does not compare training time for true versus random labels or report convergence time by corruption level.
The study does not report training on shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.

It reports MNIST experiments at specified corruption levels, but does not test the full range through 100% corruption. Test-error values are figure-only, without a textual description establishing the claimed steady rise toward chance.
The study does not test the necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation for these outcomes.
The study does not measure whether true-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

relationships.condition: Perfect training-set fitting on 1000 MNIST images with 5%, 10%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 50%, 60% or 80% randomized training labels.
relationships.reason: Based on the text rather than extracted rows: Figures 3 and S19 explicitly report 100% training accuracy under these corruption conditions, supporting V4's perfect-fitting component.
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy reached 100% at every tested corruption level from 5% through 80%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
